candidate_relations.reason: Calciphylaxis is a different retiform necrotic process and is not LMWH-induced distant skin necrosis.
HIT is a related heparin reaction but requires thrombocytopenia, which is absent (platelets 173), and omits distant-from-injection necrosis.

candidate_relations.reason: Warfarin-induced skin necrosis is a related anticoagulant skin necrosis with incompatible warfarin rather than LMWH etiology.
COVID-19-associated thrombosis is an incompatible explanation; infection was asymptomatic and lesions followed abdominal heparin, distant from inoculation.
Antiphospholipid syndrome is a different thrombotic disease; autoimmunity studies were negative.
Cholesterol crystal embolism is a different ischemic skin process, not heparin-induced necrosis.
Caliphylaxis is a spelling variant of calciphylaxis, still a different entity from LMWH-induced distant necrosis.
Purpura fulminans is a different acute septic/DIC necrosis syndrome, not heparin-induced distant skin necrosis.
Thromboangiitis obliterans is a different smoking-related vasculopathy.
Peripheral artery disease explains the admission foot ulcer, not the new distant pretibial heparin-associated necrosis.
Thrombophlebitis is a different venous process, not retiform necrotic plaques.
Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia again conflicts with a normal platelet count and is not distant LMWH inoculation-site-sparing necrosis.
Vasculitis is a different inflammatory diagnosis; autoimmunity studies were negative.

case_quality_flags: No complete_equivalent candidate states LMWH-induced skin necrosis distant from injection; platelets are 173×10^9/L, so HIT is not established.
